sections.title: Physics in Medicine
sections.description: This course examines the application of fundamental physics principles to the structure and function of the human body and to modern medical technologies. Topics include biomechanics, fluid dynamics of the circulatory and respiratory systems, energy transfer and thermoregulation, bioelectric phenomena in the nervous and cardiovascular systems, and the physics of vision. The course also introduces the physical principles underlying medical diagnostics and imaging, including ultrasound, endoscopy, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), X-ray, computed tomography (CT), single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT), and positron emission tomography (PET), and concludes with an overview of therapeutic applications such as radiation dosimetry, external and internal radiation therapy, and the use of lasers in medicine. Prerequisite: This course is appropriate for students who have completed an introductory physics sequence equivalent to PHYS0101 and PHYS0102. A physiology course such as BIOL 2301 is highly recommended. LPS Pre-Health students have priority seating.
